To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the genetic distance between two individuals is not constant in time but fluctuates in an evolving population, (ii) in a sexual population the fluctuations of the genetic distance become negligible in the limit of infinitely large population size, (iii) in a population where mating occurs only between individuals with similar genetic makeup, the population splits into species which are reproductively isolated from each other, and (iv) the behavior of the population in this model is similar to that of a disordered system

the genetic distance between two individuals in an evolving population depends on the mode of reproduction, and that the genetic distance is small for sexual reproduction with random mating, but large for asexual reproduction and for sexual reproduction with nonrandom mating.

the distribution of genetic distance between individuals fluctuates greatly in an asexual population, is very small in a sexual population with random mating, and is large in a sexual population where mating is restricted to similar individuals.
